Patch 0.31.7 (Patch Notes content uses shared entry classes)

  • Patch Notes content now uses reusable entry chrome: Release titles and bullet lists now share patch-note title and list classes instead of repeating inline heading and list styles on every entry.
  • Patch history spacing is owned by CSS: Patch note entries now get their bottom spacing from the shared patch-note-entry class instead of per-entry margin styles.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass extends inside support windows: Patch Notes now shares both its support-window shell and its repeated content styling through class-based CSS.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for patch-note entry title/list classes and removed repeated inline Patch Notes content chrome.

Patch 0.31.6 (Settings asset cache uses shared panel classes)

  • Asset cache Settings now use reusable panel classes: The cache header, status, progress meter, pack list, badges, metadata, and action row now share asset-cache CSS instead of inline layout and typography.
  • Cache action buttons now use named variants: Recommended download, refresh, update, and clear actions keep their visual intent through reusable button modifier classes instead of one-off inline color styles.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass keeps consolidating Settings: Settings now shares shell, body, footer, action-row, core field, and asset-cache panel patterns before moving on to the next client menu surface.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for asset-cache panel markup, meter styling, pack badge styling, action button variants, and removed inline cache chrome.

Patch 0.31.5 (Settings core fields use shared form classes)

  • Core Settings rows now use reusable support-field classes: Graphics quality, brightness, auto-loot, camera shake, and fullscreen controls now share field, row, label, hint, value, select, and range styling.
  • Repeated inline form styling has been reduced: The primary Settings controls no longer duplicate label colors, hint typography, row layout, or range width inline.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass keeps tightening support menus: Settings now shares shell, body, footer, action-row, and core field patterns before the asset-cache section gets its own cleanup.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for support-field markup and reusable Settings form CSS.

Patch 0.31.4 (Support menu actions use shared rows)

  • Support menu footers now share action structure: Settings and Help close areas use the shared support-window footer class, while Report now uses shared support action-row classes.
  • Report actions no longer carry one-off button widths: Cancel and Submit now use reusable support button sizing classes, and Submit uses a shared success button modifier.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass keeps reducing inline menu chrome: Support windows now share shell, body, footer, and action-row patterns before the next menu-feel cleanup pass.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for support footer/action-row classes and reusable report action buttons.

Patch 0.31.3 (Static support menus share shell and body classes)

  • Settings, Help, Report, and Patch Notes now share support-window chrome: Their modal shell sizing, viewport caps, overflow rules, and z-index tiers now live in reusable CSS classes.
  • Support menu bodies now use reusable scroll classes: Tall settings controls, help guides, report fields, and patch history content scroll through shared support-window body variants instead of one-off inline body styles.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass covers the static support layer: Static support menus now line up with the generated and pause menu cleanup direction before the later audio/accessibility work begins.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for support-window shell classes, support body scroll variants, and 0.31.3 version presentation.

Patch 0.31.2 (Pause menu joins the shared window pattern)

  • Pause menu chrome is now class-based: The Escape menu now uses reusable pause-menu and pause-menu__actions classes instead of carrying its position, width, and body spacing inline.
  • Pause actions stay reachable on short screens: The button stack now scrolls inside a viewport-capped pause menu frame when vertical space is tight.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass covers another primary menu: Pause, generated, Forge, static, service, quest, and HUD utility windows now share the same direction: viewport-safe shells with reusable body/action structure.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for pause menu viewport-safe chrome and reusable action-stack markup.

Patch 0.31.1 (Generated menu chrome now lives in shared CSS)

  • Generated menu shell styles are no longer duplicated inline: Dungeon Portal and Talent Master now let shared generated-menu classes own backdrop, position, sizing, overflow, and action-row behavior.
  • Dynamic controls use reusable class hooks: Dungeon selects, difficulty choices, and generated menu footers keep their layout through shared CSS instead of one-off JavaScript style assignments.
  • The 0.31 consistency pass gets easier to extend: Future generated menu polish can target one CSS surface instead of auditing duplicate modal shell styles in multiple UI modules.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage that generated menus use reusable chrome classes and no longer depend on inline viewport shell styles.

Patch 0.31.0 (Client UX consistency pass begins)

  • Generated menus now share consistent chrome: Dungeon Portal and Talent Master use shared generated-menu and backdrop classes instead of living as one-off modal frames.
  • Dynamic menu controls are easier to keep consistent: Dungeon selects, difficulty rows, and footer action rows now carry reusable classes that match the 0.30 viewport behavior.
  • The 0.31 line starts from the completed 0.30 sizing audit: The next client-quality work can focus on consistent headers, bodies, footers, tabs, and menu feel instead of basic clipping fixes.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for shared generated modal chrome, reusable generated action rows, and 0.31.0 version presentation.

Patch 0.30.4 (Dynamic menus now finish the viewport audit)

  • Dungeon Portal and Talent Master now respect the viewport: Generated menus now cap their height, scroll internally, and keep footer actions reachable when their guidance or option lists grow.
  • Special panels now follow the same sizing rule: Skill Tree, party roster, and party invite surfaces now stay inside normal viewport bounds instead of relying on fixed desktop-only frames.
  • Small-screen controls are harder to clip: Dungeon selectors and difficulty controls now wrap or shrink inside their menu instead of forcing horizontal overflow.
  • Regression coverage: Added coverage for generated menu viewport caps, special panel sizing, and 0.30.4 version presentation.

Patch 0.30.3 (HUD utility windows now follow viewport rules)

  • Abilities, Inventory, Character Sheet, and Split Stack now respect the viewport: The remaining HUD utility windows now use viewport-capped dimensions instead of fixed desktop-only frames.
  • Growing utility content now scrolls internally: Ability lists, character stats, inventory contents, and split-stack controls can scroll inside their windows when the available screen height is tight.
  • The 0.30 menu-quality pass is more consistent: Primary HUD, service, quest, Forge, and static menus now share the same basic rule: stay inside the viewport and keep actions reachable.
  • Regression coverage: Added regression coverage for responsive HUD utility window constraints, plus 0.30.3 version presentation.
